Em.bar_b_note: A's site-specific aftermaths (freed captive, smoking wrecked camp, revealed emblem stone) carry the idea, but smeared low-res ground, uniform grass carpet, tiled cliff wall and flat noon light with no fog or sky depth sink it beside Palworld/Valheim.

Ai.bar_b_note: The Brooktail otter is a genuinely appealing hero creature and B finally shows both fighters, but the bubble/puff effects are generic sprites, the meadow backdrop is flat and fogless, and tells still live in panel text.

Fo.bar_b_note: A warm, readable elder with clear eyes and a good green/brown palette, but the soft toy-like animated-film finish leans more cartoon than the key art's stylised realism and the costume materials are plain.

Fj.bar_b_note: B's open-field framing keeps the Mudsnout and Terrapup readable, but the small player creature, puff-cloud attacks smothering it, dark muddy grass and absent sky/fog depth keep it well short of Palworld finish (A is sunk by a gate filling the frame).

Ay.bar_b_note: The spider boss silhouette reads in B, but both sides are a dark brown-green murk with no purple storm sky, lightning or copper/glass highlights, flat magenta floor glyphs carry the attacks, and A's camera repeatedly ends up inside trunks and canopy.

Pm.bar_b_note: B's long blue-and-gold drake has a strong readable silhouette and scale over the ruler, but surface detail is thin next to the owner's furred/plated bar and A's faint end collapses into an unreadable crumpled heap.

Uz.bar_b_note: Warm brazier-lit stone hall gives the closest Valheim-style mood in the batch and B frames both fighters well, but tiled brick walls, generic puff-cloud attacks and text-only tells keep it below shipping finish.

Ys.bar_b_note: Aeriex and Cloudfang are attractive sky creatures, but A drowns the fight in speed lines, puffs and a white disc flash while B's murky blue-grey dusk grade flattens values and leaves dark player creatures on dark sand.

top_changes.change: Fix fight cameras and effects together: keep the player's creature framed and unoccluded (no gates, trunks or canopy between camera and fighters), replace white puff-cloud and disc-flash hits with grounded stone/water/spark impacts at the struck creature's feet, and give every tell a body wind-up plus an in-world (non-magenta, non-text) danger cue.

Lift the world grade to the key art: warm saturated grass with clumped groves and clearings instead of smeared uniform carpet, cool blue aerial-perspective fog and real skies in Meadows, and the purple storm sky with lightning and copper/glass highlights in Stormwood so fights are not dark mid-tone murk.
Raise creature surface quality toward the owner style bar (fur/scale/plate detail and rim light on the Pm drake, Terrapup and Bramblebun) and author readable grounded faint-end poses.
